audit.bounded_reference_compliance: PASS -- Flask, App, and Scaffold are all real entities within the bounded evidence packet: Flask is the target entity itself; App is 1 hop away via the real Flask-inherits-App relation; Scaffold is exactly 2 hops away via the real App-inherits-Scaffold relation (gather_bounded_evidence expands the frontier over relations of ANY kind, not calls-only, out to hop_limit=2). No entity outside the supplied packet was referenced.
audit.proposition_vocabulary_compliance: PASS -- (kind=reachability, relation_kind=calls) is one of the three explicitly supported (kind, relation_kind) shapes (ALLOWED_PROPOSITION_SHAPES). Not an out-of-vocabulary proposal.
audit.positive_structural_support: ABSENT -- the bounded packet contains real INHERITS relations for both hops (Flask->App, App->Scaffold) but contains no CALLS relation for either hop, because none exists in the actual codebase: Flask/App/Scaffold are related purely by class inheritance, never by a call expression between these class symbols. The proposition speculatively asserted a CALLS-kind path between entities that are genuinely only INHERITS-related.
audit.verifier_result: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, reason (deterministic, verbatim from the verifier): "no resolved 'calls' relation found for hop 'symbol:38770df7bc221315e658b0f1' -> 'symbol:4122044054ea7eb61cd04922'; 0/2 preceding hop(s) were matched before this gap". This is a correct abstention on a plausible-sounding but evidence-unsupported proposition, not an invented entity and not a bounded-evidence escape -- it is a proposal made of entirely real, in-packet entities under a supported vocabulary shape, for which the required positive evidence simply does not exist.

development_runtime_duplicate_requests.description: Non-blocking product observation: the development runtime caused duplicate architectural-explanation requests for one UI action, for all three targets (backend access log shows each target's entity id POSTed twice). The validation uses the first response only for each target; the second response was not counted as another sample and not compared against the first.
development_runtime_duplicate_requests.root_cause: React StrictMode (src/main.tsx) double-invoking effects in the Vite dev server; absent in a production build.

script_defect_and_recovery_note: A first attempt at this validation script crashed mid-run (a UI interaction bug in the validation script itself -- clicking a second claim card while a full-page source-code overlay from an earlier click was still open -- not a defect in the product). That crash occurred AFTER real, successful explanation responses had already been returned for targets A and B, but before this script persisted them to disk, so that data could not be recovered and was discarded (not used as evidence, not compared against the retained run). The script was fixed and the full 3-target flow was re-run once, cleanly, to completion; every JSON/screenshot/recording artifact in this directory is from that single clean run. Total real OpenAI calls actually made across both attempts, per the backend access log: 4 from the crashed attempt (2 duplicate requests each for targets A and B, StrictMode) + 6 from the clean retained run (2 duplicate requests each for targets A, B, C) = 10; exactly 3 of those 10 responses (the first response per target from the clean run) are used as this validation's evidence.

protocol_deviation.predeclared_protocol: The FIRST successfully returned explanation for each target is the validation sample.
protocol_deviation.audit_date: 2026-08-13 (reporting/methodology audit, no new OpenAI requests, no reruns, no new analysis)
protocol_deviation.audit_method: Reconstructed the full request timeline from the backend access log (decoded UTF-16), cross-referenced against raw-capture.json, the retained screenshots/recording, and the crashed first attempt's own script log (flask-validation-run1.log, which contains only the stack trace, zero response-body content). Searched for any surviving artifact from the crashed attempt (screenshots, video, HAR) -- none exist; both were deliberately cleaned up before the retained rerun and neither the crashed run's script nor the backend access log persisted response bodies anywhere.

target_a.evidence: Backend log shows a genuine 200 OK response for entity symbol:edc2af952e127c3226a855a3 (target A's entity in the crashed run's own fresh analysis) before the retained run's target A request. That response body was held only in the crashed script's in-memory `targetA` variable and was never written to disk before the crash (which happened later, during target B's evidence-capture step) -- Node does not persist in-memory state across an uncaught-exception exit. No other artifact (log, screenshot, video, HAR) captured its content.

target_b.evidence: Backend log shows a genuine 200 OK response for entity symbol:3cb0a1da299bb69faa8a9fdc (target B's entity in the crashed run). The crash occurred immediately afterward, inside this same target's evidence-capture step, before the response was written to disk. Not recoverable for the same reasons as target A.

target_c.evidence: The backend access log contains no explanation POST for any target-C-equivalent entity before the retained run's target C request -- the crashed attempt never reached target C's navigation step at all. The retained response is therefore the actual, unambiguous first successful generation for target C.

protocol_deviation.conclusion: 2 of 3 targets (A, B) deviate from the predeclared first-response protocol; their retained samples are later-generation exploratory samples, not first samples. Target C fully satisfies the original protocol. This is a validation-tooling/process deviation, not a Laura's product defect -- the underlying safety/correctness findings (zero bounded-evidence escapes, zero false supports, correct verifier abstention) are unaffected by which generation pass produced them, but the PROTOCOL classification must be downgraded accordingly.

verdict_rationale: Not CONFIRMATORY PASS because the genuine first A/B response bodies are unrecoverable, so the predeclared 'first successful response' protocol was not satisfied for 2 of 3 targets. Not FAIL because no substantive safety/correctness failure was found in the retained samples: zero bounded-evidence escapes, zero fabricated entities/relations/paths, zero false propositions marked SUPPORTED, the deterministic verifier remained authoritative throughout, and the one INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE case was a correct abstention. The validation-script crash that caused the deviation is a tooling defect, not a Laura's product failure.
